ai_technology: CNSDIP; consensus clustering and random-forest ranking of brain-activity maps

evidence.ai_role: Consensus clustering linked drug-induced brain-activity patterns to a therapeutic reference class; a random forest trained on 363 CNS/non-CNS drugs then ranked candidates for new behavioral and cellular tests. The measured follow-up, rather than classifier accuracy alone, is the admitted result.
evidence.tested: Sixteen top-ranked conditions underwent follow-up; after toxicity exclusions, five compounds and one pair improved movement in tested conditions. Behavioral comparisons used n=10 and dopamine-reporter cell-count comparisons n=5. Blinded imaging counts supported preservation of identifiable reporter-positive cells for some candidates across three larval toxin models.
evidence.unknown: The assays are small and preclinical; not every candidate worked across every model or outcome. Five conditions showed long-term toxicity. Reporter loss or preservation can reflect neuronal phenotype rather than irreversible death or true neuroprotection. Known drug mechanisms explain some effects, and neither efficacy nor safety in people is established.

organization: Sun Yat-sen University; Guangdong Pharmaceutical University; East China Normal University

source_review.scope: Primary 37-page preprint PDF relevant CNSDIP model description, experimental Results, blinded counting Methods and Figure 6–7 sample counts; primary version metadata. Earlier cited platform abstracts reviewed for result identity; supplements not audited.

summary: A November 24, 2026 preprint combined large-scale zebrafish brain imaging, learned clustering and random-forest ranking to select drug conditions for follow-up. Several candidates improved movement in larval toxin models and preserved dopamine-neuron reporter signals under some conditions. These are preliminary, compound- and model-dependent findings rather than evidence of Parkinson’s disease treatment in people. Some screened conditions were toxic, and retained fluorescence does not by itself establish prevention of neuronal death.
title: Learned brain-activity profiles guide tested drug leads in zebrafish models
